title: [Evals Workshop] Mastering AI Evaluation: From Playground to Production
talk_summary: A Brain Trust vendor workshop walking through their eval platform: tasks/datasets/scores, offline playground vs. online production scoring, logging via SDK wrappers, and human-in-the-loop review. Most content is product demo, but several concrete eval-design and feedback-loop mechanisms are copyable.

takeaways.technique: Split LLM-judge criteria into narrow single-purpose scorers plus deterministic code scorers
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one judge scoring many criteria, they define separate narrow judges (accuracy, completeness, formatting) and pair them with deterministic code-based checks; disagreement between the two signals a broken eval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're not overloading a single LLM as a judge score with accuracy, completeness, and formatting

takeaways.technique: Eval the judge against human ground truth
takeaways.what_they_do: Humans label a sample of outputs; those labels become ground truth to test whether the LLM-judge prompt agrees with humans, and the judge prompt is tuned until it does.
takeaways.evidence_quote: maybe you should eval the judge and make sure that the prompt that you're using is matching what a human would think

takeaways.technique: Trial evals with averaging to beat judge non-determinism
takeaways.what_they_do: Because LLM judges are non-deterministic, run each eval multiple times and average scores rather than trusting a single run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you will run it maybe five times and then take the average of those

takeaways.technique: Online scoring with sampling rate and regression alerts on live traffic
takeaways.what_they_do: Score a configurable sample (e.g., 1-100%) of production traces with the same scorers, alert when scores drop below a baseline, and tag by prompt/model variant for A/B comparison.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can decide how many logs that are coming in will get evaluated and scored

takeaways.what_they_do: Save filtered log views (e.g., score < 50%, thumbs-down feedback), then one-click add those spans to the offline eval dataset so failures become permanent regression tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: anytime my completeness score goes below 50% I want to create a view for this

takeaways.technique: Evals in CI pointing at the live task, not a frozen copy
takeaways.what_they_do: Eval files call the actual application task dynamically, so when app logic changes the eval still exercises current code; evals run on PRs and results are tracked as experiments over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you are wanting to merge into main, you open a PR and then your evals will run on those new changes
